questions.question: Why did Peter want to write a special letter just for Amy to invite her to his party?
questions.explanation: This question helps children understand that Peter wanted Amy to feel special, connecting to the idea of making friends feel important.

questions.question: How do you think Peter felt when the wind blew his letter away? Why do you think he chased it so much?
questions.explanation: This question encourages children to put themselves in Peter's shoes, linking his actions to caring about his friend and being determined.

questions.question: When Peter worried about what his friends would say about inviting a girl to his party, what would you say to him if you were there?
questions.explanation: This question asks children to reflect on the importance of not worrying about what others think when including friends, making the moral personal and relatable.

questions.question: Have you ever made a friend feel special, like Peter tried to make Amy feel special? What did you do?
questions.explanation: This question invites children to connect the story to their real-life experiences and think about ways they can be kind friends.

questions.question: How did Amy feel when Peter bumped into her and tried to hide the letter? How do you know?
questions.explanation: This question helps children notice and understand emotions, which is important for empathy and understanding how actions affect others.

questions.question: Why do you think it’s okay for everyone, including girls and boys, to be friends and celebrate together?
questions.explanation: This question opens up a conversation about inclusiveness and friendship, relating the story to real-life social situations.

questions.question: What could Peter have done after Amy ran away crying to help her feel better?
questions.explanation: This question encourages children to think about how to fix hurt feelings and be a good friend, making the moral lesson more concrete.

questions.question: How did everyone feel at the end of the story when Amy came to the party? Why do you think everyone was happy?
questions.explanation: This question focuses on the outcome of the moral lesson—togetherness and joy—helping children see the result of being inclusive.

questions.question: Can you think of a time when someone worried about inviting a friend because they were different, like Peter worried? What happened and how did it make people feel?
questions.explanation: This question helps children apply the story’s lesson to real-life situations, promoting empathy and understanding about friendship and inclusion.

questions.question: If you had a birthday party, who would you want to invite and how could you make them feel special?
questions.explanation: This question lets children imagine putting the moral into practice, making it personally meaningful.

moral: It is nice to make your friends feel special, and it’s important not to worry too much about what others might say. Everybody can be friends and celebrate together.
learning_objectives: Children will understand the importance of making friends feel special and cared for.
Children will recognize that boys and girls can all be friends and celebrate together.
Children will express their own feelings and experiences with friendship and inclusiveness.
Children will practice ways to make their friends feel happy and included.
